WaAppAgent.exe queried membership of local groups (Administrators and Remote Desktop Users), which is consistent with account discovery but could also be routine Azure guest agent functionality.

SDXHelper.exe (a legitimate Microsoft Office process) made outbound HTTPS connections to Microsoft cloud infrastructure and queried a Microsoft Office-related domain, which is consistent with normal Office functionality rather than adversarial command and control.

Administrator executed ntdsutil with the 'ifm' (Install From Media) command to create a full backup, and ntdsutil subsequently created the NTDS database file and SYSTEM registry hive in the specified backup directory.

The analyst claims the technique is T1003.008 (/etc/passwd and /etc/shadow dumping, a Linux technique), but the events show Windows NTDS credential dumping activity with ntdsutil performing raw disk reads and accessing Volume Shadow Copy on a Windows domain controller.
The analyst claims PowerShell execution (T1059.001), but the events show cmd.exe being spawned from Explorer, with no PowerShell involvement.

The events show auditpol.exe disabling DS Access audit logging, clearing the entire audit log with /clear /y, and modifying the CrashOnAuditFail registry setting to disable crash-on-audit-fail, which are direct actions to disable Windows audit logging.

The events show payload.exe was launched from explorer.exe with High integrity level and consent.exe performed a logon with explicit credentials, which is consistent with UAC elevation but does not definitively prove the AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges API was used versus other elevation methods.

The events show creation and deletion of an auditpol.exe prefetch file, but this is normal Windows behavior (prefetch files are automatically created and cleaned up) and does not demonstrate intentional evidence removal of audit policy modifications.
